correctness.rationale: On the clockwise shift eigenvalues 1,−1,i,−i the generator eigenvalues are 0, −2(a+b), and −(a+b)±i(a−b). None hits the Padé denominator poles 3±i√3 after scaling by h≥0. To check the decisive numerator identities without the uploaded checker or a Fourier inversion, I put Z=h(ax+bx³−a−b) in the polynomial ring with x⁴=1 and verified exactly that the proposed numerator N=ΣN_j x^j satisfies (12−6Z+Z²)N=D(12+6Z+Z²), and N(1)=D. Thus the four coefficients divided by D are the actual four row entries with the stated orientation. The common denominator and diagonal numerator are positive on h≥0; the opposite entry is positive for h>0. Both nearest-neighbor quartics have positive coefficients at degrees zero through three. Their leading coefficients have the signs of 3b²−a² and 3a²−b², respectively. This gives strict positivity for finite h>0 in the closed rate interval. Outside, exactly one leading coefficient is negative, and its F(h)/h⁴ decreases strictly from +∞ to that negative coefficient. It has exactly one positive root, simple, with the necessary sign on both sides. The other entries stay positive. At h=0 the update is the identity; at the horizon precisely the affected entry type is zero. These calculations establish every h, including both bias endpoints.
residual_risks: This is completed-step positivity on a constant-rate four-cycle only, not stage positivity or a variable-rate/larger-cycle assertion.

evidence: The 2010 manuscript has sufficient Padé positivity criteria and treats 2×2 Hurwitz Metzler systems in Section III-E. The 2012 Example 3 gives a negative [2/2] Padé entry at every h>0 for an eight-state nilpotent shift.

evidence: The map r(hQ) is exactly the [2/2] diagonal Padé approximation of exp(hQ). For this conservative generator it fixes the all-ones vector, so completed-step entrywise nonnegativity is equivalent to stochasticity.

value.rationale: A bidirectional homogeneous four-cycle is a natural small conservative transport model where drift can vary independently of overall time scale. The criterion gives the precise drift tolerance of a standard fourth-order integrator, and the unique horizon beyond it exactly determines the permitted step range. It resolves both an all-step boundary and the finite-step behavior across the full positive two-rate family, rather than tabulating isolated parameter choices.
residual_risks: The usefulness pertains to this homogeneous cycle and rational update; other graphs or integrators are not automatically covered.
